14 The density of water is 1.0 g cm–3 and the density of glycerine is 1.3 g cm–3.
Water is added to a measuring cylinder containing 40 cm3 of glycerine so that the density of the
mixture is 1.1 g cm–3. Assume that the mixing process does not change the total volume of the
liquid.
What is the volume of water added?
A
40 cm3
B
44 cm3
C
52 cm3
D
80 cm3

hints: Start from the $40$ $\text{cm}^{3}$ of glycerine of density $1.3$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$ and work out its mass in grams.
Remember mixture density is total mass divided by total volume, where total volume is $40 + V$ and total mass is glycerine mass plus $1.0V$.
Set $(52 + V)/(40 + V) = 1.1$ with $V$ in $\text{cm}^{3}$ and solve the linear equation for $V$.
walkthrough: Identify the knowns: $V_g = 40$ $\text{cm}^{3}$, $\rho_g = 1.3$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$, $\rho_w = 1.0$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$, and target $\rho = 1.1$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$.
Calculate the glycerine mass using $m = \rho V$: $m_g = 1.3 \times 40 = 52$ $\text{g}$.
Let the added water volume be $V$ in $\text{cm}^{3}$. Then $m_w = 1.0V = V$ in grams, total mass $= 52 + V$, and total volume $= 40 + V$ because volume is conserved.
Solve: $52 + V = 44 + 1.1V$, so $8 = 0.1V$ and $V = 80$ $\text{cm}^{3}$ with correct units of volume.
Check: total mass $= 132$ $\text{g}$ and total volume $= 120$ $\text{cm}^{3}$, giving $132/120 = 1.1$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Equal volumes of $1.0$ and $1.3$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$ would give a mean density of $1.15$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$, which is higher than $1.1$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$.

B.explanation: This is close to $40$ $\text{cm}^{3}$ plus a small change and does not satisfy total mass divided by total volume equals $1.1$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$.

C.explanation: $52$ $\text{g}$ is the mass of the $40$ $\text{cm}^{3}$ of glycerine, not the volume of water needed to lower the density to $1.1$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$.

D.explanation: With $80$ $\text{cm}^{3}$ of water, total mass $132$ $\text{g}$ divided by total volume $120$ $\text{cm}^{3}$ equals $1.1$ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$.
